title: Working the riverbank
changes: Towns with funded Irrigation can build an exact-site river intake and local plots. Each later operating season needs one Material, one remaining resident and eight available river-flow units for three base Food.

Upstream withdrawals physically reduce downstream flow. Dry or paused intakes keep their structures; receipts separate current eligibility from actual paid output. Existing Irrigation and mountain catchments remain unchanged. New worlds start fresh.

title: Rivers shaped by the land
changes: New worlds retain connected downhill drainage through their actual terrain, from inland valleys to the sea. Narrow channels join at confluences and remain part of the shared map surface.
Terrain and starting opportunities may change. River geography does not yet supply irrigation, navigation or production; this version starts a fresh autonomous world without upgrading older saves.

title: Work and study in the districts
changes: A funded Guild workshop shows a warm working doorway and compact work detail. A funded University shows a cool study window on its existing facade.

Activity follows the latest paid, staffed operation. Paused, blocked or completed-world sites keep their buildings without an active-work cue. Resource costs, research and civilization choices are unchanged.
